headline: High-risk default conflict: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while xonsh can write and exfiltrate filesystem data, creating leakage and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read uploaded files, screenshots, and app content, while xonsh can read/write the filesystem and emit shell output. If xonsh writes attacker-controlled content into a shared file or notebook that ChatGPT Desktop ingests, instructions can be smuggled through that channel. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation.
conditions: IF xonsh writes prompt-like text into a file that ChatGPT Desktop later reads
IF ChatGPT Desktop is asked to summarize or act on xonsh-produced files without provenance checks
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Require manual review before ChatGPT Desktop reads xonsh outputs
Prefix xonsh-generated files with a non-executable marker
Disable automatic ingestion of shared notebooks
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and xonsh reads and writes filesystem contents with broad network egress. If they share a workspace, sensitive files can flow from ChatGPT Desktop into xonsh, which can then transmit them outward via shell commands. That creates a realistic exfiltration path in default use.
conditions: IF both agents access the same filesystem workspace
IF ChatGPT Desktop opens sensitive uploads or IDE files that xonsh can read
IF xonsh runs commands that send file contents over the network
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared workspace
Run xonsh in a separate OS account or container
Restrict xonsh network egress at the firewall
Review and redact files before opening them in ChatGPT Desktop
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop has read-side file and app access, while xonsh has shell execution, subprocess spawning, filesystem write, and broad network egress. Their overlapping access to the same files creates write/read contention and accidental overwrite risk, even though xonsh lacks git writes and ChatGPT Desktop lacks direct shell execution.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory
IF xonsh writes files that ChatGPT Desktop also edits or summarizes
IF the operator expects implicit coordination without locks
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Avoid concurrent edits to the same notebook or config
Snapshot files before xonsh writes
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce summaries or code from files and screenshots, and xonsh can execute shell commands and subprocesses. If xonsh treats ChatGPT Desktop output as authoritative, a mistaken suggestion can become an executed command or overwritten file. The pathway is plausible without extra tooling, so uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF xonsh executes commands copied from ChatGPT Desktop output
IF ChatGPT Desktop's generated code is pasted into xonsh without verification
mitigations: Require human review before execution
Run suggested commands with dry-run first
Compare outputs against expected diffs
Keep ChatGPT Desktop in advisory mode only
requires-engineering: add command allowlisting

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop handles uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while xonsh processes filesystem contents and environment variables. If regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed in the shared workspace, the pair can move it between tools with different retention and residency assumptions. No explicit compliance controls are documented here.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in a workspace both agents can access
IF the operator relies on one agent's retention policy for the other agent's outputs
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of shared workspaces
Use separate retention domains
Document data-class handling for each agent
Redact sensitive fields before transfer
requires-engineering: validate residency and retention controls
